item.title: Help shape new European standards for electronic contracts and mediation
item.description: CEN/TC 447 is developing two new standards, one on electronic contracts and one on mediation. The TC would like to invite experts to help shape these standards from an early stage. The work will support clearer, more accessible digital contracting and promote effective mediation as a means of resolving disputes and improving access to justice. Two projects responding to changing service relationships As services become increasingly digital and contractual relationships more complex, organizations need practical guidance that supports clarity, accessibility and trust. CEN/TC 447 ‘Horizontal standards for the provision of services’ is developing two projects that respond directly to these needs: guidance on electronic contracts and a proposed European standard on mediation. item.title: Academic Standards Days in Slovenia 2026: Connecting Students, Industry and Standardization Through Real-World Challenges
item.description: On 12–13 November 2026, the Slovenian Institute for Standardization (SIST) successfully organized the fourth Autumn School of Standardization – Academic Standards Days in Slovenia – at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering of the University of Ljubljana. The event attracted considerable interest, with more than 160 participants registered and 90 students taking part in the hackathon on the second day. Students from thirteen faculties at the universities of Ljubljana and Maribor attended, reflecting the growing interest in standardization among young people from diverse academic backgrounds. item.title: Standards Norway launches new campaign: “Agreed. Since 1923.”
item.description: Standards Norway has launched a new campaign built around the concept and tagline “Agreed. Since 1923.” The campaign is part of Standards Norway’s recent rebranding and represents an evolution of the Standards Norway brand and visual identity, not the introduction of a new brand. Building on more than 100 years of history, the concept highlights the role Standards Norway has played in bringing people, businesses and industries together to find common ground and develop solutions through consensus. Since 1923, Standards Norway has helped facilitate more than 40,000 agreements through standardization – at the national, regional and international levels. item.title: CEN OSD is expanding to Harmonized Standards!
item.description: The Online Standards Development (OSD) journey continues: Harmonized Standards will soon be enabled in CEN OSD, marking another important step in the digital transformation of the CEN standards development process. Join our December and/or January CEN OSD info session to discover what is changing and for a practical recap of the full process in CEN OSD, from project creation all the way to publication. item.title: Camelia Tulcan receives the 2026 Standards+Innovation Education Award
item.description: We are delighted to congratulate Professor Camelia Tulcan, from the University of Life Sciences “King Mihai I” in Timișoara, Romania, on receiving the 2026 Standards + Innovation Education Award. The award was presented this week during the EDU4Standards event in Brussels, recognizing her outstanding contribution to bringing standardization into education through innovative teaching, practical learning and international collaboration. Camelia Tulcan has demonstrated a strong commitment to embedding international standards in higher education, research and laboratory practice. She integrates ISO standards into Applied Laboratory Science courses, giving students practical experience in applying internationally recognized standards. item.title: From Interoperability to Sustainability: The Contribution of European Railway Standards
item.description: Sustainable transport is essential to building a more connected, resilient and low-carbon Europe. On World Sustainable Transport Day, we look at how European standards help turn these ambitions into practice. Rail provides a compelling example: alongside interoperability and safety, common standards help create the conditions for more efficient and sustainable mobility across Europe. Europe’s modern railway system has been built through decades of technical and regulatory cooperation. An important first step came in 1996 with Council Directive 96/48/EC on the interoperability of the trans-European high-speed rail system. item.title: Discover the BeBOP Standardization Toolkit to explore the standards landscape behind sustainable biomethanol
item.description: The first version of the BeBOP Standardization Toolkit was officially showcased on 19th October at the ENEA premises in Brussels, during the project’s 2nd Dissemination Event. The event was dedicated to unlocking the potential of sustainable biomethanol through innovation, research, industry engagement, and standardization. Developed by UNI, the Italian Standards Body, within the framework of the standardization activities set out in the EU-funded BeBOP project (GA n. 101178117), the toolkit provides a public and interactive entry point to the standardization landscape relevant to BeBOP, turning a structured mapping dataset into an accessible, interactive resource for researchers, technical experts, industry stakeholders and other interested users.
